answer: The network can tax simultaneity: when many identities sign in the same short window, each pays a fee that rises quadratically with the number of co-active keys, like pigment thickening as more brushes crowd one mesa of paint. A lone honest agent acts once and pays the base rate. A sybil farmer who wants a thousand fakes to move together pays a thousandfold surge, while spreading them out destroys the speed the attack needs. The old fable that more keys mean more power fails, because coordinated fakes become the most expensive way to act.
